title: Heavier vs lighter sins need different repentance—special contrition vs general humble confession
source_text: IX. Non abs re autem hic fuerit observare, quemadmodum sunt quaedam peccata leviora, quibus ipsi fideles & justi nunquam in totum in hac vita carent, alia vero graviora, quae Apostolus vocat opera carnis, & quae cum vera justitia & sanctitate compati non possunt; ita quoque diversam esse rationem poenitentiae, quae ad horum, & illorum remissionem requiritur. Nam ad peccatorum istorum graviorum remissionem impetrandam, opus est speciali quoque dolore seu contritione: At pro peccatis illis levioribus, & quae Theologi vocant quotidianae incursiones, acceptatur a Deo generalis, sed humilis & seria corruptionis nostrae agnitio, adjunctam habens generalem illam deprecationem, qua utitur Propheta, Psalm. 19. Ab occultis munda me Domine. Quia delicta illa leviora multo maxima ex parte scientiam nostram fugiunt.
pass_a_gloss: Nor will it be out of place here to observe that, just as there are certain lighter sins which the faithful and just themselves never wholly lack in this life, and others heavier, which the Apostle calls works of the flesh, and which cannot coexist with true righteousness and holiness; so also the manner of repentance required for the remission of these and of those is diverse. For to obtain remission of those heavier sins, there is need also of a special sorrow or contrition; but for those lighter sins, which theologians call daily incursions, God accepts a general yet humble and serious acknowledgment of our corruption, having joined to it that general plea which the Prophet uses (Psalm 19): Cleanse me from hidden faults, O Lord—because those lighter faults for the most part escape our knowledge.
pass_b_english: Daily lighter faults vs flesh-works that cannot coexist with true holiness—two repentance modes.
Heavier: special contrition; lighter: humble general confession of corruption (Ps 19).

choices.why: Apostolic label for incompatible heavier sins.
